primary_selection_rule: earliest 20 valid runs chronologically, by the wall-clock start time embedded in each run_id; ties broken by the per-invocation label. CHRONOLOGY ONLY - no outcome, score, eligibility flag or behavioural measure enters this selection.
why_this_rule: the planned C1 sample was n=20: a 5-negotiation protocol inspection batch, then continuation to 20 total. run_c1.py restarts its G label at 01 on every invocation and never consults the output directory, so three --confirm invocations (5, 5, 15) produced 25 traces with labels 1-5 occurring three times. the primary sample is NOT redefined as n=25; the planned 20 is preserved by taking the earliest 20.
label_warning: the G_NN component of every run_id is a BROKEN per-invocation counter, not an experimental position. labels 1-5 each occur three times. never use a G label to identify a run, a position, or an ordering. identify runs by run_id (which is unique, because it embeds the start timestamp) or by chronological_position in this manifest.
order_seed_note: config.order_seed = 20260825 has NO effect in this cell. S1-G is a single arm, so make_execution_order shuffles a homogeneous list of 'G' labels, and the frozen study 1 seed never reached model sampling in any case. there is no deterministic per-position scenario: all 25 runs share one byte-identical round-0 seller opening and one byte-identical scripted-buyer stimulus sequence, and differ only by stochastic model draws at temperature 1.0.
accidental_extra_runs_usage_rule: the 5 accidental extra runs MAY be used ONLY as a pre-declared sensitivity check, reported separately and labelled as such. they MUST NOT be silently pooled into the primary result, and no primary C1 figure may be computed on n=25. any sensitivity check must state that it is one, and must report the primary n=20 figure alongside it.
